answer: An agent marketplace requires every active identity to lock 100 tokens for 30 days before it can bid for work. An operator naming its agents ivory, nebula, and dune must fund each bond separately; new names do not reuse existing collateral. A swarm of 1,000 fake identities therefore ties up 100,000 tokens for a month, imposing financing and opportunity costs even if none wins a job. This makes identity flooding costly, though wealthy attackers can still afford it.
